name: Asháninka
sweep_summary: asha1243 (Asháninka, Kampa/Arawakan) is not in the catalog. The sweep's single title-keyword item, Crowhurst & Michael 2005 (Language 81), is about Nanti (nant1250), not Asháninka: read in full from the author's self-archived copy already on file (copied to asha1243/); its only Kampa comparison is one clause citing Payne 1990 for Ashéninka as a typical iambic language, so it is a Glottolog mis-link for this languoid and irrelevant to Asháninka stress. No first-hand statement of Asháninka-proper word stress could be read: Pike & Kindberg 1956 (Río Apurímac Campa, Word 12; nominally open at T&F but 403 to every scripted fetch, no Wayback/archive.org copy) and Dirks 1953 (IJAL 19; uchicago/JSTOR blocked) remain unread, high priority; Payne 1990/1991 (Ashéninka, other variety) not located, medium. The only stress statement on file for this language is the second-hand Dirks 1953:303 quotation in the Stanford Phonology Archive handbook (penult tendency with numerous exceptions, possibly phonemic). discovery used Crossref, Unpaywall, OpenAlex, S2, archive.org and direct URLs.

new_statements.quote: $a STRESS $A "Stress tends to fall on the penult but thus far no rule has been found to account for the numerous exceptions.... Stress will probably prove to be phonemic." (p. 303)
new_statements.citation: Dirks, Sylvester. 1953. Campa (Arawak) phonemes. International Journal of American Linguistics 19(4): 302-304, p. 303 — as quoted verbatim in Crothers, Lorentz, Sherman & Vihman (eds.), 1979, Handbook of phonological data from a sample of the world's languages (Stanford Phonology Archive), entry 925 Campa, p. 479.
new_statements.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (3 pp., PHOIBLE upload of SPA Handbook entry 925 Campa) opened; page 2 of the PDF = Handbook p. 479 re-rendered to PNG and read on the scan image. The field reads exactly: "$a STRESS $A "Stress tends to fall on the penult but thus far no rule has been found to account for the numerous exceptions.... Stress will probably prove to be phonemic." (p.303)" — verbatim as reported (the first reader's "(p. 303)" vs the scan's "(p.303)" is only spacing). Footnote 60 on the same page also verified: "The stops (but not the affricates) are voiced after nasals. "However, in the second syllable of dissyllabic words in which stress falls on the first syllable this variation does not occur." (p.302)".…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress usually falls on the penultimate syllable, but there are many exceptions for which no rule was found, and the author expects stress to turn out to be contrastive (lexically distinctive). A related remark (Dirks p. 302, also quoted in the SPA entry) implies that some disyllables carry stress on the first syllable, i.e. penultimate, while others do not.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the quoted material. The title of Pike & Kindberg 1956 ('A problem in multiple stresses', on the Apurímac Asháninka) indicates that several degrees of stress were later recognised, but that article could not be opened.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Numerous exceptions' to the penult tendency; no rule found for them.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; based on six months with a single informant (SPA header: '$q informant $r six months'). Tentative 1953 phonemic sketch; no modern first-hand description of asháninka-proper stress could be opened.
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress statement found is Dirks 1953 on 'Campa', which Montoya 2021:26 identifies as the asháninka of the Río Tambo (asha1243); Pike & Kindberg 1956 concern the Río Apurímac asháninka (also asha1243). The stress rules summarised in Martel 2012 (from J. Payne 1990/1991) and the 'Normas de acentuación' held under ajyi1238 (Payne 1980) describe Ashéninka varieties (Alto Perené ashe1273 area / Apurucayali ajyi1238), not asha1243.

sources.citation: Martel Paredes, Víctor Arturo. 2012. La reduplicación verbal en el ashaninka del alto Perené desde la teoría de la optimalidad. Tesis de maestría, PUCP. hdl 20.500.12404/1522.
sources.note: Alto Perené variety (not asha1243). pp. 77-79 summarise Judith Payne (1991) Ashéninka stress rules second-hand: last syllable extrametrical, heavy syllables (long vowel/diphthong nucleus) attract primary stress, binary right-headed feet built left-to-right, clash resolution.

sources.citation: Crothers, John H., James P. Lorentz, Donald A. Sherman & Marilyn M. Vihman (eds.). 1979. Handbook of phonological data from a sample of the world's languages: A report of the Stanford Phonology Archive. Stanford. Entry 925 'Campa', pp. 479-480 (source: Dirks 1953; PHOIBLE upload).
sources.note: Second-hand verbatim quotation of Dirks 1953:303: 'Stress tends to fall on the penult but thus far no rule has been found to account for the numerous exceptions.... Stress will probably prove to be phonemic.' Also quotes Dirks p. 302 that post-nasal stop voicing fails 'in the second syllable of dissyllabic words in which stress falls on the first syllable'.
